review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked the two definitions in it that could compete with existing concepts.

- `zariskiPretopology` is `pretopology @IsOpenImmersion`. It is a named specialisation of the generic `Scheme.pretopology P` in `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Pretopology.lean`, not an independent concept. A grep over Mathlib finds no uses of it outside this file. The only one is `zariskiTopology_eq`, which relates it to `zariskiTopology`.
- `zariskiTopology` is an `abbrev` for `grothendieckTopology IsOpenImmersion`, so it is also a thin named specialisation of the generic API.
- `affineOneHypercover` is built on the existing `OneHypercover` and `refineOneHypercover` API.
- The remaining declarations are theorems or instances, which the rubric excludes. The only definitions here, apart from the two specialisations above and `affineOneHypercover`, reuse existing machinery.

I found no competing parallel definition, no duplicated API and no repeated conversions. The named specialisations are an intentional design choice, so I abstain. I am uncertain only about whether `zariskiPretopology` is worth keeping given it has no other uses. That is a dead-code question, not a duplication one.
